sources.title: Plan, test, and block if untested
claims_used: Plan the previously recommended next path before implementation.
Test and verify the plan with deliverable evidence.
Block the plan if it is not tested.

sources.title: Authoritative repository contract
claims_used: Use small evidence-bearing changes.
Write testable requirements with stable IDs and source bindings.
Qualify critical checkers with known-good and known-bad controls.
Missing evidence or unresolved architecture fails closed.

sources.title: Locked Architecture
claims_used: The state-transition service is the sole canonical writer.
Canonical commits use revision vectors and compare-and-set.
Agents operate through bounded authority and independently verified evidence.

sources.title: Verification Authority
claims_used: PASS, FAIL, and BLOCKED are distinct.
Evidence must preserve reproducible execution facts.
A critical checker must reject known-bad or mutated controls.
A producer cannot be the sole verifier of a consequential result.

sources.title: Security Authority
claims_used: Authority is deny-by-default and comes only from the Authority Envelope.
State, prompts, models, and tool visibility cannot grant authority.
External effects require evidence beyond a tool result.

sources.title: Plan Stage Contract
claims_used: Plan defines requirements, data contracts, fitness functions, evidence, and human gates.
Plan selects the smallest vertical slice that can falsify the central hypothesis.
Plan must not write production implementation.

sources.title: Problem-to-Retained-Revenue Operating System
claims_used: Stage 0 precedes optimization.
Stage 1 returns a candidate problem, not a solution.
Stage 2 requires Real, Unsatisfied, Consequential, Reachable, and Solvable.
The common operating record has 17 stable semantic fields.
Only externally evidenced exit conditions can progress business state.

sources.title: Current Developer agent
claims_used: The current runtime code defines one proposal-producing SDK agent.

sources.title: Current DevelopmentProposal contract
claims_used: The current contract does not represent the common operating record or canonical transitions.

sources.title: Building Evolutionary Architectures, 2nd edition
sources.locator: Chapter 1, Evolutionary Architecture; Chapter 2, Fitness Functions
claims_used: Evolutionary architecture supports guided incremental change across multiple dimensions.
Fitness functions make protected architecture characteristics explicit and testable.
Metrics, tests, and other verification mechanisms may serve as fitness functions.

sources.title: Interpretable Context Methodology: Folder Structure as Agentic Architecture
sources.locator: Section 3.1 Design Principles and section 3.2 Architecture
claims_used: Each stage has one job and writes to its own folder.
Markdown and JSON are inspectable stage interfaces.
Stable reference material is separate from per-run working artifacts.
Every intermediate output is an editable human surface.

sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.locator: Section 1.2.2 Risk Tolerance and Core functions GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE
claims_used: Risk tolerance is contextual and should be defined by the responsible organization.
Development or deployment should cease safely when risk is unacceptable until it is managed.

sources.title: The Definitive Guide to LLM App Evaluation
claims_used: Pre-production evaluation uses controlled inputs and golden datasets.
Production behavior requires separate online evaluation.

selection_note: Repository authority supplies requirements. Provided references supply planning rationale only and cannot override repository or human authority.
